Appellant/owner of the offending vehicle has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 assailing the impugned award dated 29/1/2007 passed by Member, Motyor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jaura, District Morena in Claim Case No. 20/2006; whereby, respondent No. 1/claimant has been awarded a compensation of Rs. 85,600/- for the injuries received by him in road accident dated 11/1/2004.

sentences.text:
Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 11/1/2004 when respondent No. 1/claimant after selling vegetable was going on his cycle by the side of the road to his village, it is alleged that due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No. 2/driver the road roller dashed the cycle of respondent No.
1 from behind due to which he sustained grievous hurts in his left leg, which gave rise to filing of claim case claiming compensation to the tune of Rs. 29,25,000/- which has been allowed in part by impugned award and a compensation of Rs.
85,600/- has been awarded.

4. It is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that on the fateful day, the road roller was moving on road in snail pace and no accident has happened due to negligence of driver of road roller, instead it was the respondent No. 1 who could not apply the brake in type and his cycle collided with the road roller.
Further the injury sustained were simple in nature.
Further Claims Tribunal erred in not believing the statement of witness produced on behalf of appellant as DW/1-Raghav Mittal.
No independent witness has been examined on behalf of the respondent No. 1 and therefore, Claims Tribunal erred in solely believing the version of respondent No. 1.

No certificate regarding permanent disability by the treating doctor has been produced and therefore,
Claims Tribunal erred in believing the statement of doctor who prepared the permanent disability certificate.
Income of injured as assessed by the Claims Tribunal is on the higher side and amount awarded under the other heads is also on the higher side.

5. On the other hand, by filing cross-objections, respondent No. 1 has sought enhancement in the compensation amount as according to her due to injuries, claimants has to undergo treatment for long period and due to permanent disability suffered, he is unable to perform his daily works as well as business activities as he was performing prior to accident.
The income of injured as assessed by the Claims Tribunal notionally is bad in law as he was earning Rs. 3,000/- per month prior to accident .
The amount awarded under the conventional heard is on the lower side looking to the period of treatment.
6. None appeared on behalf of respondent No. 2 to contest the appeal.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the impugned award.
8.

This is an appeal on behalf of owner of the offending vehicle which is a road roller in the instant case challenging the impugned award whereas in the appeal, cross-objections have been filed on behalf of respondent No. 1 seeking enhancement in the amount of compensation..
9. It is not in dispute in the instant case that from the offending vehicle the accident was caused in which respondent No. 1 suffered fracture of tibia fibula bone of left leg.
10. Only dispute in the instant case is who is responsible for the accident.

As per respondent No.
1/claimant the offending vehicle dashed his cycle from behind; whereas, as per the opposite party,
due to mistake of respondent no. 1 himself, his cycle collided with stationed road roller.

sentences.text: In support of his evidence, respondent No. 1 examined himself and his version is not refuted.
FIR was lodged on the same day of accident and police filed challan finding mistake of respondent No. 2 for causing the accident.
In rebuttal no evidence was produced.
Even respondent No. 2 not entered the witness box to state that it was respondent No. 1 himself, who was responsible for accident.
Further the witness produced on behalf of appellant is not an eye witness to the accident.

And thus,
in the opinion of this Court, learned Claims Tribunal did not err in accepting the version of respondent No. 1 and holding that due to mistake of respondent No. 2, accused caused.
12.

From Ex. P/22 disability certificate and the statement of Doctor H.S.Dandotiya, it is clear that due to alleged accident, respondent No. 1 suffered permanent disablement as left leg of respondent No. 1 got shortened by 1/2 cm after the treatment of fractures; however, from such disablement, in the opinion of this Court, there was no adverse effect to respondent No. 1 in his business of selling vegetable and considering overall facts and circumstances of the case especially the fact that accident caused in the year 2004, in the opinion of this Court, the amount of award, as awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper which needs no interference.

Cross-objections are therefore,
rejected.
13. Cumulatively, in view of aforesaid discussion, appeal also sans merits and is hereby dismissed.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
